images.title: One fact, three answers
images.purpose: Show that one whole number product gives the digits of several related decimal products and quotients.
images.composition: One highlighted fact box at the top centre with three arrows fanning down to three answer boxes in a row, generous white space between boxes.
exact_structure: 1 reddish purple #CC79A7 outlined box at the top centre: '45 × 12 = 540'
3 grey #6B7280 arrows from the top box down to 3 boxes in a row
Under the left and middle boxes a small grey note: '2 decimal places'
rejection: a number of answer boxes other than 3
the decimal point misplaced in any box
images.takeaway: The digits come from 45 × 12 = 540; counting decimal places, or scaling both numbers in a division, places the point.
images.description: The fact 45 × 12 = 540 at the top with arrows to 4.5 × 1.2 = 5.4, 0.45 × 12 = 5.4 and 54 ÷ 1.2 = 45.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on using one fact to find many answers.
images.teaching_notes: Cover the answers and ask whether each is nearer 5, 50 or 500 before uncovering.

image_decisions.why: A fan of answers from one fact shows that the digits stay and only the point moves.
